## CANDIDA KRUSEI
C. krusei is resistant to fluconazole, and often has some degree of resistance
to amphotericin. Higher doses of amphotericin are recommended for treatment of
C. krusei due to decreased susceptibility.
## Duration of antimicrobial therapy
Duration of therapy is dependent upon location and severity of infection,
and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.
## Preferred treatment
## Inpatient

[Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h ($$$) [H,DI]](psjizid-micafungin-100mg-iv-q24h)
*150mg q24h for esophageal candidiasis, 100mg q24h for other indications
< OR >
## Alternative
[Voriconazole 6mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,H,DI]](psjizid-voriconazole-6mg-kg-q12h-then-4mg-kg-iv-q12h)
< OR >
[Voriconazole 400 mg PO q12h for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO q12h ($$) [R,H,DI]](psjzid-voriconazole-400mg-po-q12h-then-200mg-q12h)
< OR >Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for IV options.
